stem: Parents of a 12-year-old ask how to set limits without damaging independence. Which advice best matches the recommended parenting approach?

options.text: Stay emotionally distant but enforce strict rules consistently
Be warm and involved, set firm consistent boundaries, and adapt as the young person matures
Let the adolescent make all major decisions to speed up autonomy
Avoid boundaries so conflict stays low
Focus on obedience rather than psychological autonomy

explanation: Be warm and involved, set firm consistent boundaries, and adapt as the young person matures. This approach supports healthy adolescent development by combining warmth, clear limits, and increasing autonomy over time.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect because effective parenting in adolescence includes warmth and involvement, not emotional distance.
optionExplanations.B: Correct because the recommended approach combines warmth, firm and consistent boundaries, and flexibility as the young person develops.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because autonomy should increase gradually, but parental guidance and boundaries remain important.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because avoiding boundaries does not provide the structure adolescents need for healthy development.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because the focus is on fostering psychological autonomy, not simply demanding obedience.
